test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements with regard to the Green Revolution is NOT true?

options.text: It requires decreasing inputs over time.
It uses high-yielding varieties of seeds.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It requires decreasing inputs over time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The introduction of new, high-yielding varieties** into emerging countries starting in **the middle of the 20th century, **led to a significant increase in the **production of food grains (particularly wheat and rice).**
 
• **Mexico and the Indian subcontinent **saw their first stunning successes.
 
• In order to achieve their high yields, the new types need to use significant quantities of chemical fertilisers and pesticides, which raises concerns about the expense and potential negative impacts on the environment. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The collection of research and technology transfer programmes** known as the** "Green Revolution" **took place between** 1950 and the late 1960s and significantly enhanced agricultural** production throughout much of the world.
 
• High-yielding varieties (HYVs) of cereals, particularly dwarf wheat and rice, were adopted as a result of the initiatives.
 
• It was connected to** mechanised farming, artificial fertilisers, agrochemicals, controlled water supply (typically using irrigation), and innovative farming techniques.**
 
• These were all considered to be part of a** "bundle of activities" that would replace "conventional" technology and be adopted as a whole. **
